answer: These guides explain the rules and choices behind the calculators in plain English: net billing and the buyback rate, peak and off-peak hours, the FPA line on your bill, lithium versus tubular batteries, and whether a home needs a UPS or an inverter. Each guide links to the calculator that works out your own numbers.

p: The [[D11|net billing guide]] explains how new solar connections are billed and how that compares with the old net metering. The [[F13|peak hours guide]] lists peak and off-peak timings for time-of-use meters, and the [[F14|FPA guide]] explains the monthly fuel price adjustment line and who is exempt from it.

The [[H8|lithium vs tubular battery]] guide compares usable energy, life and cost, and the [[H9|inverter vs UPS]] guide explains switching speed, waveform and solar charging. To price the choice for your own backup hours, use the [[N7|UPS vs solar vs generator cost calculator]].

faq.q: What is the difference between net metering and net billing?
faq.a: Under net metering, exported units cancelled imported units at the same rate. Under net billing, imports are billed at the slab rate and exports are bought at a flat buyback rate, so an exported unit is worth much less. New connections are on net billing.

faq.q: What is the FPA on my bill?
faq.a: The fuel price adjustment: the per-unit difference between the actual and the reference fuel cost of a past month, decided by NEPRA. Every home pays it except lifeline consumers, protected homes included; the [[F14|FPA guide]] shows how to check the line.

Lithium can be used to about {{d.dod_lifepo4|pct}} of its rating against about {{d.dod_lead_acid|pct}} for tubular and lasts more cycles, but costs more to buy. Which works out cheaper depends on how much backup you use; the [[H8|guide]] compares both.

faq.q: UPS or inverter for a home?
faq.a: Both turn battery power into AC during a cut; they differ in switching speed, size, waveform and whether they charge from solar. The [[H9|inverter vs UPS guide]] explains which suits a home.
